prediction.likelyOutcome: 721 is likely to prevail on liability under the CRD addendum given Montagnet's own trial admissions, but is likely to recover something less than the full $106,077.89 repair invoice because CRD has a credible, evidence-supported argument that the ADA-driven asphalt resurfacing exceeded the contractual repair obligation and constituted a capital improvement. The lost-profits, attorney's-fee, and interest components of the prayer remain unsupported by any figures in the record and are unlikely to add materially to the judgment absent further proof at trial.

outcome.description: After a one-day bench trial the court found CRD liable for damage during both leases and awarded 721 all of its claimed repair costs, $106,077.87 (no lost-profit award is described), then awarded $51,770.71 in attorney's fees and judicial interest. The Fourth Circuit affirmed liability but held Gibbs and CRD solidarily liable for the Gibbs-period damage, amended the judgment to reduce the damages by 50% for the settled co-obligor's virile share, and reversed the attorney's fee award because the lease did not provide fees for a Clause 13 breach.
outcome.finalNote: Reduced on appeal to a 50 percent share.
